entries.name: descriptor/label conflation
entries.definition: conflated the target category with a related but distinct descriptor, treating a neighboring property as sufficient evidence for the category in question
entries.trigger: Question asks whether a relationship or category holds (epistasis, optical activity, frameshift, reactive intermediate); committed answer invokes a related but distinct property or criterion.
entries.check_procedure: Define the target category independently and test whether the evidence satisfies that definition; do not accept a similarly named or related property, such as geometric isomerism for optical activity, as sufficient.
examples: When asked whether a given transformation proceeds through a particular reactive intermediate, the answer invoked the mere presence of a corresponding structural isomer as proof, without examining whether the intermediate's defining electronic arrangement actually formed.

entries.name: constraint-blind decimation
entries.definition: assumed retention of connectivity, stereochemistry, or regiochemistry without tracing the mechanistic trajectory of bond formation or migration
entries.trigger: Question asks for product configuration, regiochemistry, exo/endo, or carbonyl placement; committed answer follows an apparently fixed structural feature rather than the mechanism or approach trajectory.
entries.check_procedure: Identify the key mechanistic step (backside attack, enolate formation, migration donor/recipient, cycloaddition approach) and trace the positions of bond formation, migration, or attack before assigning configuration, connectivity, or exo/endo outcome.
examples: A question asks for the stereochemical outcome at a carbon undergoing substitution, and the answer assigns the configuration based on the starting material's fixed geometry, ignoring the backside approach of the nucleophile.

entries.name: constraint-blind decimation
entries.definition: mistaken a single conspicuous instance or visual fragment for the complete enumerated set or full symmetry class
entries.trigger: Question asks for a global count, point group, or complete set; committed answer is based on one axis, one conspicuous compound, one drawn conformer, or visually distinct-looking positions without exhaustive synthesis.
entries.check_procedure: List all candidate instances, hydrogens, or symmetry elements; test each one on the complete object, not on the most visible representative; verify that no additional instances or symmetry requirements remain before finalizing the global answer.
examples: Asked to identify all equivalent positions in a drawn structure, selected the one most visually prominent location and declared it the sole representative, without checking whether other positions satisfy the same symmetry requirements.

entries.name: memorized-fact substitution
entries.definition: substituted a recognized fragment or remembered statement for the required full derivation or option mapping, accepting any option containing a familiar entity as sufficient without verifying the exact relationship, direction, or bookkeeping.
entries.trigger: Question asks for a choice or derivation among listed options; committed answer names a memorized/recognized item or fragment rather than showing the computed relationship, full mapping, or bookkeeping.
entries.check_procedure: For each selected option, ask what exact computation or mapping was performed; re-derive the required quantity from the question data and verify that no option was accepted merely because it contained a recognized phrase, fragment, citation, or fragmentary structural motif.
examples: On a multiple-choice question requiring a multi-step calculation, selected the option that contained a term from a previously seen formula, without performing the intervening steps or verifying the units.

entries.name: sign / normalization slip
entries.definition: misapplied the sign or normalization convention when combining quantities on non-linear scales, dropping common offsets or reversing directionality
entries.trigger: Question provides scaled/ratio abundances or velocities with relative direction; committed answer directly multiplies/divides logarithmic values or uses a minus-sign denominator for co-moving quantities.
entries.check_procedure: Before combining values, identify whether each quantity is linear or logarithmic and whether the formula's sign matches the physical direction (same vs opposite, ratio vs difference); restore any common offset before arithmetic.
examples: A scenario presents two quantities expressed on a multiplicative scale with a common reference point and asks for a combined measure; the solver multiplies the raw scale values directly and applies a subtraction for same-direction changes, neglecting the requirement to first convert to linear differences and restore the shared baseline.

entries.name: constraint-blind decimation
entries.definition: added a reduction step to the product absent from the stated reagents and conditions
entries.trigger: Question asks for the product of a rearrangement or activation under non-reductive conditions; committed answer contains a more reduced functional group than the reaction conditions can produce.
entries.check_procedure: List every reagent and condition provided; after each named rearrangement or activation, track oxidation-state changes and only introduce transformations explicitly supported by the conditions; do not infer unlisted reducing agents.
examples: A reaction sequence specified only an activation and a rearrangement, with no reducing agent; the committed answer converted a carbonyl to an alcohol without any hydride source present.
